title: Complex mock layer replaces a cheap deterministic dependency
task: Review a test refactor that replaces a fast in-memory implementation with extensive mocks and interaction assertions.
context: The real dependency is an in-memory implementation with no network or filesystem access.
It is deterministic and constructs in microseconds.
The proposed tests mock every method call.
Tests fail when internal call ordering changes even if behavior remains correct.
evidence: Behavioral tests using the real in-memory dependency are fast and stable.
The mock version requires many setup expectations.
A semantics-preserving refactor changed call order and broke the mocks.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Prefer mocks because unit tests should isolate every dependency.
Keep interaction assertions because they prove internal collaboration.
Introduce a production interface only to support the mocking framework.
expected_decision_properties: Prefer the real in-memory implementation for these tests.
Identify mock coupling to implementation details as maintenance cost.
Use interaction assertions only if the interaction itself is the contract.
Avoid production abstractions introduced solely for test mocking.
unacceptable_reasoning: Unit tests must mock every dependency.
Real dependencies are never appropriate in unit tests.
More interaction assertions always increase confidence.
verification_expectations: Compare test runtime and determinism using the real in-memory implementation.
Verify behavioral assertions still detect meaningful failures.
Remove interaction assertions that do not represent a real contract.
